newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - M&G shares hit as H1 profits disappoint.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - M&G shares hit as H1 profits disappoint.

text.p: Fund management group M&G Group Plc said on Thursday its underperforming UK unit trust business had constrained first-half profit growth to six percent.

Analysts said they would be downgrading profit forecasts for the group's full-year earnings amid concerns about non-recurring costs in the second half but said longer term prospects were positive providing their UK equity business came good.

The group said a project for its systems to cope with the millennium date change was expected to be completed by the end of 1998 at a cost of five million pounds ($8.2 million) over the next 18 months.
Other costs relate to windfall personal equity plans (PEPs) and some non-recurring costs related to relaunching its UK equity unit trust products later in the year.
Earnings were held back by relative underperformance in some of its unit trusts, but that it believed its value investment approach remained fundamentally valid.

"We think these results have demonstrated the basic resilience of the business because it is a style that has not done well...it has not been an easy environment for us," group managing director Michael McLintock told Reuters.
Pre-tax profits were 33.2 million sterling from 31.2 million a year earlier, while the interim dividend was left unchanged at 16 pence.
Analysts told Reuters they expected pre-tax earnings to come in at between 68 and 75 million sterling for the year, representing a cut in previous forecasts above 76 million.
A small increase in the dividend was expected at the full year stage.

"It is not all doom and gloom in the sense that some of the downgrade will relate to them quantifying the cost of the millennium project and they have also indicated the timing in the second half of the reorganising of their unit trust stable," said UBS analyst Martin Cross.
McLintock said there was room for improvement in the group's investment process and fund range.
"We think the prospects for value are actually pretty good in this market but we always think there are ways we can improve what we do," he said.

M&G is looking at its fund range, and plans proposals to unitholders in a few months about clarifying the identity of some funds. "Part of the review is looking at areas where there are gaps in the fund ranges as well as where there are overlaps."

He said institutional business had picked up since the end of the first half with about 250 million sterling in new business since the end of March, although it was difficult to predict its effect on results.
M&G also said there were early signs of a pick-up in its UK equity unit trusts which usually foreshadowed improvement more generally in its value style.
He said there was no significance about leaving the dividend unchanged.
There were good prospects on the institutional side, as well as international opportunities but this would not distract from the need to refocus the local product.

M&G has funds under management of some 16.1 billion sterling, up six percent on a year earlier. About 70 percent of this is in the UK, seven to eight percent in fixed interest and the balance international.
About a third of funds under management are institutional.
M&G's share price fell sharply on the profit announcement, trading 61.5 pence lower at 12.84 stg by 1230 GMT. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
